name: Jie Long
description: Jie Long (接龙, connect dragon) is a Chinese domino connecting game. Players extend a single open end by playing a matching tile or discarding one face down. The player with fewest pips on discarded tiles wins; pairs settle by pip difference.

history.origins: Jie Long (接龙, connect dragon) is a Chinese domino connecting game; the name likens the chain of connected tiles to a dragon. Chinese dominoes date to the 12th or 13th century (earliest written mention in Hangzhou); the 32-tile set with civil and military tiles is traditional. Published rules and table traditions describe it as a single-arm game where a player unable to play must discard one tile face down, and the player with fewest pips on discarded tiles wins the deal. Related connecting games with the same discard-when-unable mechanic exist in Korea (Golpae) and Indonesia (Gaple).
timeline: 20th century: documented in published rules and table play traditions.

setup.deck: 32 Chinese dominoes (11 civil tiles x2, 10 military tiles x1; no blanks).
setup.dealing: Four players: 8 tiles each. Three players: 10 tiles each, two tiles unused. Two players: 16 tiles each. First player for the first deal is chosen randomly; thereafter the winner of each deal plays first. Play is counter-clockwise.
setup.equipment: Chinese domino set or domino cards.

rules.objective: Play tiles matching the single open end of the layout or discard when unable; the player with fewest total pips on discarded tiles wins the deal. Pairs settle by pip difference (stake per pip agreed in advance).
rules.gameplay: First player leads any tile and declares which end is open. Each turn, in counter-clockwise order: play a tile matching the open end (the other end becomes the new open end; if a double is played the open end stays the same) or discard one tile face down. Discarded tiles are kept in front of the player until the end. When all tiles are played or discarded, players expose discards and count pips. Fewest pips wins; that player leads the next deal. Tie for fewest: whoever played earlier in the deal (previous first player has priority, then to the right).
keyRules: 32 Chinese dominoes; single open end; extend in one direction only.
Each turn: play a tile matching the open end or discard one face down.
Winner is the player with fewest pips on discarded tiles; pairs settle by pip difference.

strategy.basic: Discard high-pip tiles when you must discard; keep a variety of halves in hand to maximize the chance of playing when it is your turn.
strategy.intermediate: Play defensively. Lead high tiles like 6-6 or 6-5 to force others to discard; keep variety of halves so you can match when the turn returns.
strategy.advanced: The 2 half has only seven tiles total; attack by leading 5-2 with 2 open, then playing 2-2 to force another round of discards. Short suits can be monopolized or duo-polized.
tips: Agree stake per pip before play.
Keep variety of halves to maximize chance of matching.
Settle per pair by pip difference.

scoring.description: After all tiles are played or discarded, each player exposes discarded tiles and counts total pips. The player with fewest pips wins the deal. Each pair of players settles by pip difference; stake per pip is agreed in advance; the player with more pips pays the player with fewer.
scoring.winCondition: The player with fewest total pips on discarded tiles wins the deal and leads the next. Tie: whoever played earlier in the deal (previous first player has priority, then to the right).
